title: A Thorn for the Spire
premise: Ada Nakamura, a mercenary bound to a silent god and trapped in a valley where magic cannot enter, takes in a feral child who speaks the First Tongue — the language of dragons and covenants. The child is the last living seal on the broken pact between realms, hunted by those who profit from its ruin. Ada must carry the child out of her godless sanctuary into a world of dying dragon-fire, choosing between the loyalty she swore to her vanished god and the truth of what he did to break the covenant. In the end, Ada reforges the covenant with her own blood as the price of survival, becoming the new seal herself — mortal, magicless, and finally free.
about_author: Ada Nakamura is the pen name of a former field linguist who spent a decade documenting dying languages before turning to fantasy. She writes about borders — between tongues, between gods, between who we were and what surviving makes us.

chapters.title: The Valley That Swallows Magic
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. A child arrives half-dead at Ada's door, speaking a language older than any kingdom, pursued by riders wearing the sigil of Ada's own silent god. When the riders cross the valley's edge, their magic dies and they become merely men — and Ada kills them anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant guardianship; the first crack in Ada's safe, numb exile.

chapters.title: What the Silent God Swore
chapters.summary: POV: Ada, with interludes in the child Mira's fragmented memories. Deciphering Mira's First Tongue, Ada learns the valley isn't a refuge but a prison her god built to hide the last seal — and that his silence began the day he broke the covenant. Riders' kin gather beyond the border. Emotional beat: betrayal; loyalty curdling into questions Ada can't unask.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire, Guttering
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Ada and Mira. Fleeing the valley, they reach the Spire where the last dragon burns itself out sustaining the failing covenant. The god's church offers Ada a bargain: kill the child, restore her god's voice, return to her old life. At the Spire's heart, Mira begins to burn as the seal fails. Emotional beat: climax — Ada chooses truth over every oath that kept her alive.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Spire
chapters.summary: POV: Ada. Refusing both church and god, Ada uses the mercenary brand on her arm — her god's own mark — as the thorn that anchors the new covenant, binding herself into it in Mira's place. The dragon dies grateful; the god speaks once, only to say goodbye. Mira lives, human and free. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance; Ada returns to the valley no longer a prisoner but a keeper.
